name: Luigi Oddero Barolo Rocche Rivera 2010
text:
## Luigi Oddero Barolo Rocche Rivera 2010

**The story.** Figli Luigi Oddero is a traditional Barolo house. Its winemaking team has a direct lineage to the great [Bruno Giacosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Giacosa): winemaker Dante Scaglione, who worked with Giacosa, and his protégé Francesco Versio ([SommSelect](https://sommselect.com/products/2010-figli-luigi-oddero-barolo-rocche-rivera)). The wines are raised in the classic way, in large Slavonian oak casks (*botti*).

**The wine: Rocche Rivera.** Rocche Rivera is a "cru within a cru" in [Castiglione Falletto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castiglione_Falletto): a 2.5-hectare parcel on the sunny upper part of the Scarrone hill, right next to the famous Rocche di Castiglione and sharing its steep, sandy limestone soils. SommSelect describes a wine of "transparency and mineral intensity more akin to Grand Cru Burgundy than the bruising power of its peers". The 2010 spent three years in large Slavonian *botti* ([SommSelect](https://sommselect.com/products/2010-figli-luigi-oddero-barolo-rocche-rivera)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [Piemonte vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/piemonte) calls 2010 "outstanding: a classic vintage with plenty of acidity, firm but ripe tannins and near-perfect balance in many wines". A wet spring caused irregular fruit set, but [Nebbiolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebbiolo)'s small, thick-skinned berries proved resilient; August was hot with cool nights, and early-September rain allowed slow, steady ripening.

**What the critics say for 2010.**
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 95** (Monica Larner, on release, as quoted by [SommSelect](https://sommselect.com/products/2010-figli-luigi-oddero-barolo-rocche-rivera)). From "light, well-draining limestone soils", "a beautiful expression with loads of finesse and intensity. This is my favorite of the flight thanks to the great sense of varietal character": balsam herb, ginger, medicinal herb, blue flowers and spice in seamless integration.
- **SommSelect** (merchant's note on a library release). Dark mentholated cherries, savoury spice and mineral grip; at 16 the tannins have evolved "into a fluid, aristocratic powerhouse" just entering its prime, with 10 to 15 more years of evolution.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 92.4** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is sixteen years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2018 to 2025, but SommSelect, tasting a library bottle, thinks it is only now entering its prime, with 10 to 15 years ahead. Traditional, *botti*-aged Barolo from a great year usually rewards patience, so this is a good time to open one, with no rush. Decant gently, an hour or two ahead.

**Serving and food.** Serve at 16 to 18°C. Try brasato al Barolo, roast game birds, [tajarin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagliolini) with truffle, or mushroom risotto.

**Value and where to buy.** Oddero is well stocked here: BC Liquor has Rocche Rivera at $255.99 and Specola at $181.99; BSW Liquor has Rocche Rivera 2009 ($255), 2015 ($180) and 2021 ($250), Vigna Rionda 2007, 2015 and 2016 ($220 to $300), Specola 2021 ($170), Barbaresco Rombone 2021 ($84) and Langhe Rosso Convento ($28.49).

**From the history books**
- **Barolo's villages.** Barolo is made in Barolo, Castiglione Falletto and Serralunga d'Alba and parts of eight other communes, south-west of Alba ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barolo)).
- **Tradition and modernism.** Traditional Barolo fermented on its skins for weeks and aged for years in large casks; in the late 20th century modernists turned to shorter macerations and small barriques ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barolo)). Oddero stays on the traditional side.

**Barolo through the ages**
- **Sweet before it was dry?** It was long believed Barolo was a sweet wine until the mid-19th century, because Nebbiolo ripens so late that cold cellars stopped the fermentation, and that [Count Cavour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camillo_Benso,_Count_of_Cavour), mayor of [Grinzane Cavour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grinzane_Cavour), brought in the Frenchman Louis Oudart to make it dry. Research by Kerin O'Keefe credits instead Paolo Francesco Staglieno, Cavour's oenologist at Grinzane from 1836 to 1841, whose "Staglieno method" fermented the wine dry ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barolo)).
- **"The wine of kings, the king of wines."** The new dry Barolo became a favourite of the nobility of [Turin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turin) and the ruling [House of Savoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Savoy) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barolo)).
- **From merchants to growers.** By the mid-20th century large merchants dominated, blending grapes from across the zone; in the 1960s growers began bottling their own wines and single vineyards, and in 1980 Barolo became one of Italy's first DOCGs, with Barbaresco and Brunello ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barolo)).
- **The Barolo wars.** In the 1970s and 80s a group of producers, led by Ceretto, Paolo Cordero di Montezemolo, Elio Altare and Renato Ratti, began making more modern Barolo, with macerations of days rather than weeks and small new oak barrels, to tame Nebbiolo's harsh tannins. Traditionalists kept to long macerations and years in large casks ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barolo)).

**Curious details**
- **The last 36 bottles.** SommSelect says it bought the last 36 bottles of the 2010 in U.S. circulation for its members ([SommSelect](https://sommselect.com/products/2010-figli-luigi-oddero-barolo-rocche-rivera)).
